## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Kalyāṇadhammajātaka* (Ja 171) is a narrative discourse in the Pali *Jātaka* collection, rendered in English as *A Fine Reputation* [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. In the edited text of the *Jātaka*, the story opens with the verse incipit *Kalyāṇadhammo ti* [Fausböll 1879]. The narrative framework records that the Buddha related this story while staying at the Jetavana monastery near Sāvatthī, occasioned by the circumstances of a deaf mother-in-law (*badhirasassu*) and a devout, faithful householder (*kuṭumbī*) of Sāvatthī who had taken the three refuges and maintained the five precepts [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879].
No cross-canonical parallels in Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan traditions are recorded for this text on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus reports no cross-language parallels with a score of 10 or higher [DharmaNexus]. Within Pali literature, DharmaNexus records internal text reuse with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (*Dutiyo bhāgo*), sharing two matching passages (309 characters, with segments §1.1–3.1 of Ja 171 aligned with commentary sections §369–374_0 at a similarity of 0.92) [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral notes four translations into four languages [SuttaCentral].
